entities.summary:
Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus (unknown–unknown) was a pivotal figure in the late Roman Republic, playing a key role in shaping the course of Roman history. As a scion of the illustrious Lutatius Catulus family, Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus was groomed for politics from a young age. He gained notoriety as a defender of the capital during the civil war between Julius Caesar and Gaius Lepidus in 77 BC, earning the agnomen Capitolinus for his bravery. Following his father's consulship in 102 BC, Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus sought to emulate his family's legacy by pursuing a career in politics. Despite his prominent position, Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus remains somewhat of an enigma, with his life and legacy shrouded in mystery.

Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus's defense of Rome against Lepidus marked a turning point in the conflict, solidifying his reputation as a skilled military commander and politician. His actions during this period had a lasting impact on the Roman Republic, contributing to the eventual rise of the Roman Empire. Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus's significance extends beyond his individual achievements, as his family's influence continued to shape Roman politics for generations to come.

The legacy of Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus is a testament to the enduring power of family, politics, and military prowess in shaping the course of history. His story serves as a reminder of the complexities and challenges faced by leaders in ancient Rome, a civilization that continues to captivate and inspire scholars and historians alike.

The valor and strategic acumen demonstrated by Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus during his defense of Rome against Lepidus have been immortalized in the annals of history, earning him a place alongside other notable figures of the Roman Republic.
